full_judgment:
2. Facts relevant for disposal of this Rule, in short, are that the petitioner, as plaintiff, instituted Title Suit No. 2 of 1996 in the Court of learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), 2nd Court, Shariatpur, against the opposite parties, as defendant, for declaration of title and partition praying separate saham stating inter alia, that CS khatian No. 61 measuring 3.7 acres of land stand recorded in the name of Sabdar Sarder, Aminnesa, Emannesa and Khatunnesa out of which, they settled 0.51 acres of land from plot No. 144 to one Mubiullah as mentioned in the remark Column of relevant khatian. Sabder Sarder got 1.20 acres of land in the said CS khatian against his six annas share who died leaving wife Asha Bibi, son, the plaintiff and a daughter, Moyna. Subsequently, Moyna died leaving daughter Fatema and her husband Nayan Sikder along with the plaintiff and his mother Asha Bibi. Aminnesa died leaving Emannesa and Sabder Sarder, a sister's son by Mominnesa. In this way, Emannesa got 1.20 acres of land and Sabder Sarder inherited 1.13 acres of land. RS khatian No. 202 and 3 SA khatians for the land under Mouza Nagerpara stand recorded in their names wrongly giving share partially. CS khatian No. 9 containing 3.30 acres of land under mouza Pashimerchar belonged to Sabder Sarder and Emannesa. CS khatian stand recorded in their names and they settled 0.74 acres of land in plot No. 68 with Muhibullah as appearing from remark column in the said CS khatian. Sabder Sarder possessed 1.29 acres of land under plot Nos. 150, 17 and Emannesa possessed 1.29 acres of land under plot No. 150, 17 and Emannesa possessed 1.25 acres of land of Plot No. 16 and 18. Sabder Sarder inherited 0.78 acres of land in 2nd schedule from his father and sister Moyna Bibi, but Emannesa gifted 1.20 acres of land under schedule-1, 0.621/2 acres of land under schedule-2 and 0.74 acres of land under schedule-3 in favour of Surjaban Bibi a daughter of Aytunnesa. 

 3. The plaintiff got 0.621/2 acres of land from Emannesa through his father and in this way he got 1.401/2 acres of land in 2nd schedule. 3.39 acres of land under mouza Vadra Chap belonged to Sabder Sarder in 6 annas share, Aminnesa in 6 annas share and Emannesa in 4 annas share as recorded in CS khatian. They settled 0.94 acres of land from plot No. 159 with one Jabber Ali Sikder, Sabder. Sarder possessed 1.40 acres of land of plot No. 149 and 0.5½ acres of land of plot No. 201 and he inherited 0.88 acres of land from his father and sister. Emennesa gifted 0.27 acres of land out of 0.54 acres under plot No. 150 and 0.47 acres of land under plot No. 169 in favour of Surjaban. Aminnesa died leaving behind a sister Emannesa and Sabder Sarder, son of Mominnesa. RS and SA record partially recorded in the name of Asha Bibi wrongly, who transferred .58 acres of land to one Abdul Haq and Abdul Jalil by a registered deed dated 5-8-1964. Subsequently, said Abdul Haq and Abdul Jalil executed a deed of relinquishment in favour of plaintiff on 24-2-1965. 

 5. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint contending inter alia, that the plaintiff has no cause of action; the suit is barred by defect of parties stating that 3.19 acres of land under CS khatian No. 9 and 3.39 acres of land under CS khatian No. 76 originally belonged to Sabder Sarder, Emannesa and Aminnesa and after death of Aminnesa, Sabder Sarder and Emannesa became the owner of the property. The said owners by a registered partition deed of the year 1926 got the property partitioned between them and by the said partition deed Sabder Sarder got in total 6.32 acres under 6 khatians and Emannesa got 5.53 acres of land under 5 khatians. Emannesa by a deed of gift No. 2079 dated 29-11-1933 gifted her entire property to her granddaughter (daughter's daughter) namely Surjaban and handed over the possession of the property as per deed of partition. RS and SA record stand recorded in the names of Surjaban, her legal heirs and in the name of other transferee. 

 7. The defendant Nos. 4-7, 11, 13, 16-20, 22-24, 26, 28, 31, 37-39, 41-46, 48-50 contested the suit by filing separate written statement stating that the predecessor of the defendants purchased 0.65 acres of land from Nayan Sikder by registered kabala and also got 0.14 acres of land of CS plot No. 15 from the plaintiff by way of exchange and these defendants have been enjoying and possessing the same raising dwelling houses and cultivating the nal land. Said Nayan Sikder inherited the said land from his wife Moyna Baru who died leaving behind him as husband, son Kashem and daughter Fatema. Kashem died leaving his father Nayan Sikder and sister Fatima. RS and SA khatian stand recorded in their names. Accordingly, 0.79 acres of land separately recorded in SA khatian No. 181. RS khatian No. 202 in the name of these defendants. Therefore, the property in question by a deed of partition of the year 1926 and subsequently, by separate record of right stood partitioned among the co-sharers. As such, the present suit for declaration of title as well as partition is not maintainable in law. 

 8. The trial court framed as many as 7 issues for determination of the dispute. In course of hearing the plaintiff examined four witnesses as PWs and the defendant examined five witnesses as DWs. Both the parties submitted certain documents in support of their claim which were duly marked as exhibits. The trial court upon hearing and considering evidences on record decreed the suit in part declaring title of the plaintiff over 3.35 acres of land under CS khatian No. 61, 9 and 76, but refused to give a decree for partition by its judgment and decree dated 17-11-1997. 

 12. He finally submits that the trial court rightly decreed the suit in part declaring title of the plaintiff in the property in ejmali, but the appellate court upon misconception of law, as well as misreading of the evidences on record in one hand reduced the share of the plaintiff, and on the other hand set aside the judgment of the trial court. Referring to the relevant khatian for the property, he submits that the record of right establishes that the said deed of partition of the year 1926 has not been acted upon and the khatian also not prepared in line with the said deed of partition. As such, the trial court righty held that the partition deed of the year 1926 never saw the daylight and acted upon at any point of time. Therefore, the suit for declaration of title and the partition is well maintainable in its present form. 

 14. It is also argued that the suit property covered by CS khatian Nos. 61, 9 and 76 along with other property were partitioned between the predecessor of the plaintiff and defendants i.e. Sabdar Sarder and Emannesa Bibi by a registered partition deed dated 22-11-1926 (exhibit-C). By the said deed entire property belonged to Sabdar Sarder and Emannesa were partitioned by metes and bounds and subsequently, SA khatian also stand recorded separately in the names of the plaintiff and the defendants predecessor in respect of land of Nagerpara and Paschimar char mouza, although the SA khatian in respect of Vadra-chap mouza was published jointly. But in the said khatian, share of the parties has been clearly written mentioning specific possession of the parties in the remark column against the plot. As such, not only by deed of partition, but also from record of right it is amply established that the property was partitioned among the owners of the property and for such partition co-sharership of the parties has put an end for all practical purpose irrespective of separation of joma. In support of his such contention he has referred to the case of Aktaruzzaman Shaheen vs Abdur Rashid Khan, reported in 62 DLR (AD) 250. 

 16. It is also argued that the plaintiff claimed title in the property, claiming to be a heirs of Aminnesa as son of Sabder Sarder brother of the deceased. But according to Muslim Law of Inheritance brother's son does not inherit any property in the presence of full sister. As such, on the death of Aminnesa, Emannesa as full sister got her share as reflected in the partition deed of the year 1926, as such, the appellate court rightly observed and held that the plaintiff is entitled to get 2.90 acres of land under three khatians and he may file a properly constituted partition suit against the persons who inherited the property from Sabdar Sarder or acquired the property by purchase from the heirs of Sabdar Sarder, but they cannot claim the property got by Emannesa by the partition deed and seek any relief against the subsequent owners of the property through Emannesa. 

 19. As stated by both the parties that there has been a deed of partition dated 22-11-1926 (exhibit-C). Recital of the partition deed clearly described that on the death of Aminnesa, Emannesa, 2nd part of the deed got entire property left by her sister and admitting the position as stated in the deed of partition both Sabdar Sarder and Emannesa executed and registered the same partitioning all their properties with specification and following the said deed Emannesa subsequently, by a registered deed of gift No. 2079 dated 29-11-1933 gifted her entire property to her granddaughter Surjabannesa. Subsequent to the said transfer, relevant khatians also stand recorded separately in the name of Surjaban except the property under mouza Vadrachap. The plaintiff though claimed that the said partition deed has not been acted upon, but failed to substantiate such claim by any evidence either oral or documentary and, as such, on the basis of a statement made in the plaint and made on oath, a registered deed of the year 1926 cannot be construed as not acted upon in the absence of any contrary evidence from plaintiff side. If we consider the existence and validity of the partition deed executed and registered in between Sabdar Sarder and Emannesa, in that case, it can be easily construed that the suit property was amicably partitioned between the co-sharers and by the partition deed co-sharership between the parties has come to an end, therefore, a suit for partition of the property making the persons as principal defendants who are claiming title through Emannesa is not at all maintainable in law. 

 20. From perusal of partition deed (exhibit-C), this Court finds that the property was partitioned giving specification of each plot and as per said partition Sabdar Sarder possessed and enjoyed the property until his death and thereafter, the plaintiff along with other co-sharer of the suit property and they also made inter transfer of the property left by Sabdar Sarder, not left by Emannesa. As such, had there been any cause of action for partition of the property, the plaintiff may institute a properly constituted partition suit against the persons who claims title through Sabdar Sarder bringing all the property left by him into hotchpotch and also making all the co-sharers through Sabdar Sarder as principal defendants and the persons whose names appearing in the khatian jointly as proforma defendants in the suit. But in the instance suit the plaintiff though claimed that the partition deed of the year 1926 has not been acted upon, but no relief has been sought for, against the said deed either by way of declaration or by any prayer for cancellation of the same. In the presence of a partition deed of the year 1926 executed and registered in between the predecessor of the plaintiff and the defendants the property fell in the share of Emannnessa, and thereafter, owned by the defendants cannot be subject matter for partition which were already partitioned in between the co-sharers in the year 1926.
